parts:
Dear all,

Apologies for breaking your code with the recent ggplot2 package. I
think the best solution for now is to withdrawal ggplot 0.9.0 from
CRAN. I'll re-upload it on March 1 giving everyone some time to
respond to the changes.

If you'd like to try out your package with the development version of
ggplot2, the easiest way is to use devtools:

install.packages("devtools")
devtools::install_github("ggplot2")

If you'd like help figuring what breaks, please join the ggplot2
development mailing list (http://groups.google.com/group/ggplot2-dev),
and we'll help you out, either by providing a fix to your code, or by
fixing the underlying problem in ggplot2.

Sorry for not anticipating this problem - I didn't realise how much
ggplot2 had grown in popularity since the last time I released a new
version.

Hadley

On Fri, Jan 27, 2012 at 9:51 AM, hadley wickham <h.wi...@gmail.com> wrote:
> Dear Uwe,
>
>> Hadley, we asked you several times to sort these things out before uploads
>> to CRAN! Hence we are rolling back the former version of ggplot2 for now
>> until most of these issues are solved prior (!) to the update, please.
>
> How I am supposed to ever do anything new if I must ensure that every
> package that relies on my package does not break? I agree that I
> shouldn't break code in my own packages, but how I am supposed to
> ensure that I don't break code in everyone else's packages?
>
> You are pushing me ever closer to just releasing ggplot3, and giving
> up on CRAN's broken dependency checking mechanism.
>
> Hadley
>
>
> Dear maintainers of other packages that depend on ggplot2,
>
> I am really sorry that my update to ggplot2 has broken your previously
> working code.  However, I am only one person, and I don't have the
> resources to ensure that every version of ggplot2 is perfectly
> backward compatible with the previous version (even if I did have the
> resources, I'd have no idea how to do it while improving ggplot2).
>
> Unfortunately the package versioning system in R is fundamentally
> broken because a package can  not depend on a specific version of
> another package, only on the most recent version.  This is the root of
> the problem, and means the only way I can add new features/fix bad
> design is to change the name of the package. I am loathe to do this,
> but the CRAN maintainers are leaving me little choice.
>
> Hadley
>
> --
> Assistant Professor / Dobelman Family Junior Chair
> Department of Statistics / Rice University
